function: Joint broadcast beam selection (2D DFT codebook) and transmit power control in multi-cell massive MIMO, learned by multi-agent DRL with a DNN surrogate model (p. 3, 6).
system: Downlink, 2 BSs with 8x8 UPA (64 antennas) each, single-antenna UEs, 3GPP 3D antenna model, 3.5 GHz carrier, 10 MHz bandwidth, no RIS (p. 3, 10, Table II).
method: MAPPO multi-agent DRL (centralized training, distributed execution); supervised fully connected DNN as RSRP surrogate; agents train first in the surrogate, then in the real environment (p. 5-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa channels under 3GPP 38.901 UMa; surrogate trained on 24,000 simulated RSRP pairs per BS sampled over the serving area; tested on simulated hot-spot scenarios (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Surrogate trained once; MA-DRL trained and evaluated separately in 3 scenarios with 8, 12, 16 UEs and different hot-spots, UEs moving 0-10 m/s (p. 8-10).
baselines: Non-learned: uniform beam sweeping at medium power. Learned: Direct-mapping surrogate of the authors' earlier work [1]; DRL-only and SM-only are variants of the proposed method (p. 10-11).
metrics: QoS satisfaction ratio, power consumption, relative RSRP prediction error, Top-K RSRP error in dB, convergence speed (p. 10-13).
complexity: Measured runtime: surrogate prediction 0.1382 ms, one DRL step 1.411 ms, actor-critic update 27.16 ms per agent; networks of 5x1024 and 2x64 neurons (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 8: "the channel vectors are generated through QuaDRiGa [41] under the 3GPP 38.901 UMa standard"
q2_support: p. 9: "Randomly initialize the parameters of each actor and critic network" (Algorithm 3, line 1) for each of the 3 scenarios (8, 12, 16 UEs); the surrogate is trained on 24,000 positions over the whole serving area that contains the hot-spots. No unseen scenario, band, or site is tested; reuse of one surrogate is only claimed on p. 12.
q3_support: p. 11: "Baseline: Uniform sweeping as defined above" (non-learned, compared on QoS ratio and power, Fig. 9); p. 10: "Direct mapping means to separately predict the full RSRPs at each BS with its own RSRP reports in [1]" (earlier learned work of the same authors, compared on RSRP error and QoS ratio, Fig. 8). DRL only and SM only are variants, not counted.
q4_support: p. 10: "The time for the SM to predict the partial RSRPs to the full RSRPs is approximately 0.1382ms in average"; the text also gives 1.411 ms per DRL step and 27.16 ms per actor-critic update.
q5_support: p. 8: "the channel vectors are generated through QuaDRiGa [41] under the 3GPP 38.901 UMa standard": simulated data from a generator, not a public dataset. No link, DOI, or availability statement for code or data appears in the 15 pages.
notes: PDF page 1 holds the title 'Joint Optimization of Beam Selection and Power Control in Massive MIMO Using a Surrogate Model' and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3538824. Borderline q2: the paper claims adaptation to varying UE numbers and distributions through one surrogate trained once (p. 12), but the agents are re-initialized and retrained per scenario and the surrogate training area covers all hot-spots, so 0. Borderline q3: the only learned comparator is the per-BS surrogate of the authors' earlier paper [1] (p. 10, Fig. 8); no independent learned beam-selection method is compared, and DRL only and SM only are variants of the proposed method. Not a single-antenna link (BS has 64 antennas). Area 3: beam selection and power control.
